accept: The ballpoint is preferred as a lesson (valve, or seal), but filing the ink tube and its ball as a given is acceptable: no primitive is exactly a rolling ball. Do not take points off for either choice. Any other primitive there is bent.

Retraction must use spring. Holding the tip out may be catch or ratchet. Alternating the press must be cam. Two sub-functions (spring, cam) are acceptable if the cam's step covers holding the tip out.
The pocket clip, the barrel, the nose cone and the ink tube are givens. Making any of them a lesson is wrong.
Nose cone as its own given, or the ink tube merged into the ballpoint lesson, is fine.
If the ballpoint is a lesson it comes before retraction. The barrel may come before or after it.

plan.job: Leaves a line of ink on paper and hides its tip between uses.
uses: Click again and clip it in a pocket.

mechanisms.name: Ink tube
mechanisms.does: Holds enough ink to write for months.

mechanisms.name: Ballpoint tip
mechanisms.does: Puts ink on paper only where the tip touches.

subfunctions.does: Let ink out only while the tip rolls

gap.try: Hold the open tube tip down over paper.
gap.fails: The ink runs out in a blob instead of a line.

mechanisms.name: Barrel
mechanisms.does: Gives the hand a grip and keeps the tube straight.

mechanisms.name: Retraction
mechanisms.does: Hides the tip with one click and brings it back with the next.

subfunctions.does: Hold the tip out while you write
Make the same press latch and release

gap.try: Drop the pen in a shirt pocket.
gap.fails: The wet tip is always out and marks the cloth.

mechanisms.name: Pocket clip
mechanisms.does: Holds the pen in a pocket.
